stillExists: YES — three sound masters run for the 2026-27 cycle and the admission calendar is published annually. Programmes: 'Master Son Studio', 'Master Son Sono', 'Master Cinéma Son'. No statement of closure; a 2027 intake should be expected on the same recurring pattern.
awards: A real second-cycle master's degree of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles (École supérieure des Arts), 60 credits for Son Studio / Son Sono. Not a certificate or non-degree diploma.
entryQuote: "The majority of 60 or 120 credit masters organized at IAD are open to students holding a bachelor's degree (or equivalent)." No disciplinary restriction is stated, but selection is on file + portfolio + audition, so the discipline is irrelevant next to the artistic evidence.
liveAudition: YES — DECISIVE. "Candidates selected based on their files and work are subsequently auditioned by a jury between mid-August and mid-September." Auditions are held in person at Louvain-la-Neuve; dates are emailed to shortlisted candidates. This is an audition/jury, not merely a portfolio review or a written exam.
portfolioSpec: "a portfolio of completed works that demonstrate your technical and artistic aptitudes in the chosen orientation" — orientation-specific guides define the exact content; no universal count/length is published on the general master admission page. PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED (per-orientation guide PDFs not machine-readable).
costForTunisian: Minerval full rate: "Les frais d'inscription au tarif plein sont de 1194 € par année académique." PLUS the Belgian droit d'inscription spécifique for non-EEA students: €4,175 per year, payable by 31 January. Total ≈ €5,369/yr. Admission auditions themselves are free: "Les inscriptions aux entretiens et auditions pour l'accès aux masters sont gratuites." Minimum €50 deposit by 31 October, balance by 31 January.
fundingHeCouldWin: The €4,175 non-EEA supplement is waived for nationals of UN Least Developed Countries and for countries on the ARES list — TUNISIA IS NOT AN LDC, so he does NOT get this waiver. Other exemptions (refugees, long-term residents, Wallonie-Bruxelles International scholarship holders) do not apply to a fresh arrival. Effectively NO funding.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE pattern (2026 cycle): applications 04 May – 14 August 2026; admission commissions 24 August – 11 September 2026. Expect the same May–August window in 2027.
languageOfInstruction: French. No specific certificate level is published on the master admission page — UNVERIFIED as to the exact certificate demanded; Belgian ESA practice normally requires B2/C1 French for non-francophones.
verdictWhy: An in-person jury audition in Belgium between mid-August and mid-September is a hard gate he cannot pass with no portfolio and no audio experience, and it falls barely three weeks before term — impossible to combine with a Tunisian student-visa timeline. He would also pay the full €4,175 non-EEA supplement on top of €1,194 minerval with no scholarship route, because Tunisia is not on the LDC exemption list. Nothing here is funded and everything here is gated on artistic evidence he does not have.
correction: The record says gate = 'Portfolio only'. WRONG — IAD explicitly auditions shortlisted candidates before a jury. The record's cost band 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is also WRONG for a Tunisian: the €1,194 minerval is only the EEA rate; a non-EEA student pays an additional €4,175/yr droit d'inscription spécifique, giving ≈€5,369/yr.

acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE — leaning NO for direct M2 entry, plausible for M1.
entryQuote: The department page lists: "étudiants ayant un Master I en musique, en arts numériques, ou équivalents" and students with other Master I qualifications who can demonstrate "un bon niveau en musique, ou/et en pratique artistique numérique"; required qualifications include "une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation". His software-engineering BSc satisfies the 'culture scientifique / programmation' half outright but not the 'bon niveau en musique ou pratique artistique numérique' half.
liveAudition: NO LIVE AUDITION. portfolioSpec: No numeric portfolio specification is published (no count, length or format). Selection is dossier + interview + listening commentary. Capacity: "Effectif maximum de la promotion : 20 étudiants". UNVERIFIED as to any formal portfolio requirement.

So a Tunisian pays the differentiated master rate under décret n°2026-385 — reference €3,941/yr — plus the CVEC (~€105), not the ~€250 national rate. fundingHeCouldWin: UNVERIFIED — no programme-level funding published. Generic routes only: bourse du gouvernement français via Campus France Tunisie, or Eiffel (institution-nominated, master's age cap 25 — he is 24–26, so he may age out).

languageOfInstruction: French, fully in person ("Présentiel") at the Campus Rachais in Lyon. No specific certificate level published on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED.

institution: Ionian University
programme: MA Sonic Arts and Audio Technologies (ΔΠΜΣ «Τέχνες και Τεχνολογίες του Ήχου») — inter-departmental, Dept of Music Studi…
stillExists: DOUBTFUL FOR 2027. The programme has run since 2018-19, but the most recent call published on its own site (music.ionio.gr/sonarts/gr/call/) is still the "Προκήρυξη 2022-2023", and the Greek Ministry of Education register entry (studies.minedu.gov.gr, programme_id 1254, "Audio Arts and Technologies") reads "No Open Calls — Check back later". The founding regulation (ΦΕΚ 4677/2018, dated 18 October 2018) states the programme operates for eight academic years from inception — i.e. through 2025-26 — with continuation subject to legislation. Nothing confirms a 2027 intake. Treat as possibly lapsed.
awards: A real second-cycle Greek degree while it ran: "Το ΔΠΜΣ απονέμει Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (Δ.Μ.Σ.) στις «Τέχνες και τις Τεχνολογίες του Ήχου»" (Article 2 §3). Ministry register: 3 semesters, 90 ECTS. Two specialisations: Ηλεκτροακουστική Καλλιτεχνική Δημιουργία (Sonic Arts) and Εφαρμοσμένη Ηχητική Παραγωγή (Audio Technologies). Capacity 30/year, 15 per specialisation.
entryQuote: "πτυχιούχοι τμημάτων Μουσικής Τεχνολογίας & Ακουστικής, Φυσικής, Πληροφορικής, Ηλεκτρονικής" are listed alongside music graduates. The regulation lists eligible first-cycle fields as sound art, music art/science, sound technology, physics, informatics, engineering, and applied sound in media/culture/entertainment. A software-engineering BSc maps onto 'Πληροφορικής'.
liveAudition: NO LIVE AUDITION. "Υποψήφιοι ... θα κληθούν για συνέντευξη από τις Επιτροπές Αξιολόγησης" — an interview before an evaluation committee, held in person or online. File review plus interview, no performance test.
portfolioSpec: Optional supporting material rather than a fixed specification: "Λοιπά στοιχεία ... που να τεκμηριώνουν την υποψηφιότητα όπως ... φάκελος καλλιτεχνικών έργων" (a portfolio of artistic works among other supporting documents). No count, length or format is prescribed. Effectively UNVERIFIED as a hard spec.
costForTunisian: "Τέλη φοίτησης ... συνολικού ύψους 2.700,00 €" — €2,700 TOTAL for the whole 3-semester programme, payable in a lump sum or in three instalments. Greece charges no separate non-EU rate for this ΠΜΣ. This is genuinely cheap.
fundingHeCouldWin: Two published routes, both automatic-on-merit rather than separate applications: up to 30% of admitted students are exempted from the whole fee under Article 35 of Law 4485/2017 (means/merit tested), and the top-performing student each semester receives a €900 merit scholarship (one semester's fees). Scholarship holders must provide support services to the departments. No age cap.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE only: "από την 1η Ιουλίου 2022 μέχρι και την 18η Σεπτεμβρίου 2022" — a July-to-September window, with interviews after 18 September. No 2027 call published. UNVERIFIED for 2027.
languageOfInstruction: GREEK. "Η γλώσσα διδασκαλίας είναι η ελληνική, με κάποια μέρη ... στην αγγλική" — Greek, with some parts in English. The ministry register confirms language of instruction: "Greek". A certificate of at least good knowledge of English is additionally demanded ("Τίτλο πιστοποίησης τουλάχιστον καλής γνώσης της αγγλικής").
verdictWhy: The teaching language is Greek and he has no Greek — that alone ends it, whatever the €2,700 total fee and the informatics-friendly entry list might suggest. On top of that the programme may no longer exist: its own site still shows the 2022-23 call, the ministry register shows no open calls, and the founding regulation's eight-year term expires with 2025-26. Do not build a 2027 plan on this.
correction: The record's cost band 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr' is WRONG in unit: €2,700 is the TOTAL for the whole 90-ECTS programme, not per year. The record's gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' overstates it — there is no exam and the portfolio is optional supporting material; it is a file review plus an interview. And the record does not flag the two decisive facts: instruction is in GREEK, and no call has been published since 2022-23 (this record duplicates index 31 — same programme, two departmental URLs).

institution: RTU Liepāja Academy, Riga Technical University (formerly Liepāja University — LiepU merged into RTU on 1 Marc…
programme: New Media and Audiovisual Art (MA) — "Sound Art and Electronic Music" specialisation (joint programme with RISEBA, in c…
stillExists: YES at RTU, but the joint structure has shifted and the record's source URL is a decade stale. RTU still lists the academic master's programme "Jaunie mediji un audiovizuālā māksla" (code HMJ) at RTU Liepājas akadēmija with two specialisations, "Digitālā māksla" and "Skaņas māksla un elektroniskā mūzika", accredited 04.10.2023–05.10.2029 under certificate No. 2023/36A, taught in English, 120 credit points, 2 years, with admissions for 2025/26. RISEBA's own current master's page, however, now advertises "Audiovisual and Immersive Technology Arts" with strands in Digital Storytelling and Immersive Technologies — Sound Art and Electronic Music is NOT among RISEBA's listed specialisations any more. The sound strand now sits on the RTU Liepāja side.
awards: A real second-cycle academic master's degree in the field of Arts (akadēmiskais maģistra grāds), 120 KP / 2 years, state-accredited to 05.10.2029.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE — and the published route for a non-arts bachelor is demanding.
entryQuote: The RISEBA-side statement of the same joint programme requires either "a bachelor's degree or a second-level professional higher education diploma in the humanities or arts" plus English B2, OR "a bachelor's in social sciences, engineering, or computer science" WITH "professional artistic experience as an author or self-employed individual working in the creative industries" of 12+ months plus relevant humanities coursework. He has the computer-science bachelor and none of the 12 months of professional creative-industry practice. The 2016 RIXC page's loose "a bachelor's or master's degree ... young artists ... anyone interested in this program" wording is obsolete and should not be relied on.
liveAudition: NO LIVE AUDITION. The published process is submission of a prospective master's thesis project plus a creative portfolio, an English-language entrance examination, and an entrance interview (the 2016 RIXC text calls it an "entrance exam (online interview)"). No performance test.
portfolioSpec: From the (obsolete) RIXC call: "the application of the master's topic (up to 1 A4 page)" and "artistic portfolio (up to 5 works selected)". RISEBA's current page requires "a prospective master's thesis project application in advance, along with a creative portfolio" without a numeric spec. Current-cycle spec: UNVERIFIED.
costForTunisian: UNVERIFIED for RTU Liepāja specifically. RTU's central tuition-fee page returned HTTP 403 and the programme PDF is behind Microsoft login. Reference points only: the 2016 RIXC call quoted "3100 EUR per year" for self-funded places (obsolete, pre-merger); RISEBA's current comparable master quotes "4700 EUR" per year for non-EU students. Latvia also now requires proof of living expenses of 9,400 EUR/year for an international student residence permit from 1 January 2026. DO NOT budget on the €3,100 figure.
fundingHeCouldWin: The 2016 call mentioned 5 state-funded (budget) places — Latvian state-funded places are as a rule reserved for Latvian/EU citizens, so he should assume he is NOT eligible. No programme scholarship for non-EU students is published. Effectively UNVERIFIED / none identified.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE, from the obsolete RIXC call: applications "until August 7", entrance exam "August 10". No 2027 dates published. UNVERIFIED.
languageOfInstruction: English (RTU lists the programme as taught in English; RISEBA's variant is "English (full-time evening studies)", Thursday/Friday 18:00–21:00 and Saturday 10:00–15:00). English B2 is required; the RISEBA route adds an English entrance examination.
verdictWhy: For a computer-science bachelor the published route demands 12+ months of documented professional creative-industry practice as an author or self-employed creative, which he does not have — the arts-bachelor route is the easy one and he is not on it.
